Josie will use one of these measures of tidiness:
• look at the work herself and decide whether each student’s work is tidy or not
• ask the student to rate the tidiness of their work on a scale of 0 (untidy) to 5 (very tidy).

parts.label: (i)
parts.text:
Explain one problem about validity or reliability that Josie could have with one of her
measures of tidiness.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text:
Explain one problem about ethics that Josie could have with one of her measures of
tidiness.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
The hypothesis that Josie is testing is correlational.
Explain which one of the measures of tidiness in part (a) is not suitable for Josie to use in her
correlation.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Josie’s data shows that students who enjoy lessons more have tidier work.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text: Explain what Josie will conclude about her correlation.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text:
Explain whether Josie can conclude that having tidier classwork influences students’
enjoyment of lessons.

text: Josie is collecting data from other students in her class to test the hypothesis ‘There is a
relationship between tidiness of classwork and enjoyment of lessons’.

text: Dr Gao is planning a longitudinal study about changes in reading habits. She will study the same

creative activities (such as art, music or dance) help people to sleep well.
